A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BED-LLM research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original 20 Questions experiments, simulated-user film recommendations, model-mismatch tests and diagnostic analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original results for both tasks and reports additional baseline and ablation experiments in Table 1 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3.1 changes the stated candidate-question procedure from independent sampling in v1 to joint sampling in v2. The prior–likelihood construction, EIG estimator, hypothesis filtering, retention and uniform weighting remain.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Animals, Celebrities and Things in 20 Questions and MovieLens-100K-derived film-preference profiles. Matched and mismatched questioner–answerer scenarios are retained. Different backbone models do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated Split, ICL Beliefs and Implicit Maximization comparators. Data–Estimation participation expands beyond v1's single Qwen2.5-72B/Celebrities comparison. Entropy remains a distinct comparator rather than being renamed Split; Naive QA is simply renamed Naive.

E3.justification: The 20 Questions model lineup replaces Mistral-Large with Llama-3.1-8B. v2 Appendix E specifies temperature 1 for preference-hypothesis generation, whereas v1 Section 3.3 states 1.3. Target counts, user counts, turn budgets and candidate-pool sizes remain. These are reported setting revisions; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 directly tests replacing filtered beliefs with in-context beliefs and replacing explicit EIG computation with prompted question selection. It also broadens the joint-factorization ablation. The model-mismatch tests and hypothesis-collapse example remain, but v1 Appendix E.1/Figure 11's EIG-by-turn diagnostic is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard errors across 100 targets per 20 Questions dataset and 200 preference profiles, retaining the same success-rate uncertainty formula. Additional result rows follow this existing practice; no new seed, repeated-run or significance-testing procedure is documented.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for the new comparators and Llama-3.1-8B while removing Mistral-Large results. Retained Table 1 entries also change: Qwen/Animals BED-LLM goes from 94% to 95%, and GPT-4o-mini/Celebrities Entropy from 53% to 55%. Qwen/Celebrities Data–Estimation changes from 39% in v1 Figure 4 to 34% in v2 Table 1. Some preference curves also change. These are revised reports, with setting revisions preventing an unqualified same-setting performance comparison.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1 Section 3.2's explicit finite-sample bias discussion, O(N^-1/2) convergence-rate statement and MLMC qualification, retaining only a conditional convergence observation. The principal EIG mathematics and belief-update alignment analysis remain, often relocated or equivalently reformulated.

C1.justification: v1 explicitly highlights targeted candidate-query generation among its principal innovations. v2's abstract, introduction and conclusion concentrate the contribution framing on model factorization, belief updating and EIG estimation. The central deployment-time BED approach, novelty claim concerning proper EIG, and benefits on both tasks remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets similar Split/Entropy performance as evidence that nondeterministic likelihoods help through the proper EIG objective, and explains why good candidate samples alone cannot replace explicit optimization. It removes the interpretation accompanying v1's EIG-by-turn diagnostic. Most existing applicability boundaries and model-mismatch discussion are retained.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the 0.2 filtering threshold, exact hypothesis-generation and user-profile-generation prompts, and shared hyperparameters across models. Conversely, it removes v1 Appendix D.2's checkpoint repository identifiers, dated GPT model identifiers and chat-template information. These materially alter reproducibility documentation without establishing that every newly documented detail is an implementation change.

R1.justification: v2 refines prior-work comparisons around Split, distinguishes Wang et al.'s meta-training and Chan et al.'s calibration requirements, and adds potential complementarity with policy-based BED. Several references are removed, including Goda et al. (2022) and Rainforth et al. (2018). The central research positioning and most cited work remain.

P1.justification: The introduction, background, method explanations and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten and condensed. Detailed algorithmic discussion, the former Section 4.4 analysis, related work and experimental settings are reorganized into thematic appendices with a new contents page.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands from three to seven method columns. Separate matched/mismatched experiment figures are merged into compact grids, with changed colors, legends, axes and panel arrangements. v2 adds a fuller ablation plot and prompt displays, reformats existing prompt figures, and relocates the EIG illustration into the appendix.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct controls separating the effects of belief filtering and explicit EIG selection from candidate generation. v2's ICL Beliefs and Implicit Maximization ablations, additional Split comparator and broader factorization comparisons substantially strengthen evidence for these central design choices. The clearer organization also helps assessment. Removing exact model identifiers and the EIG diagnostic loses useful detail, but these drawbacks do not outweigh the stronger experimental validation.
